questions.question_text: When creating a new help desk ticket in a ticketing system, which basic information is typically required during the initial data collection phase? (Select 3 answers)
questions.explanation: Initial intake needs the affected user, device, and a clear problem description; escalation level is decided after triage.

questions.question_text: A technician is logging a new support ticket. Which item is primarily used to ensure that future reporting can track the frequency of specific, recurring problems?
questions.explanation: A consistent category makes recurring issue frequency measurable in reports.

questions.question_text: A support ticket regarding a system memory failure has been moved from Level 1 to a Level 2 hardware specialist. This action is documented using which specific ticketing system field?
questions.explanation: The escalation-level field records movement from first-line support to a specialist tier.

questions.question_text: A desktop technician is updating a support ticket with the steps performed to troubleshoot a network printer. Which field should contain a factual, concise summary of these steps?
questions.explanation: Progress notes are the factual running record of troubleshooting actions; the resolution summary documents the final outcome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of maintaining a chain of custody?
questions.option_a: To provide a step-by-step log of the incident remediation process
questions.option_b: To track the movement of corporate assets for inventory management purposes
questions.option_c: To track which systems were affected during an incident
questions.option_d: To preserve the integrity of evidence for potential legal proceedings
questions.explanation: Chain of custody proves who controlled evidence and helps preserve its integrity for legal or disciplinary review.

questions.question_text: Which items must always be included when documenting a chain of custody? (Select 2 answers)
questions.option_a: Description of the location where the evidence was found
questions.option_b: Method used to collect the evidence
questions.option_c: Chronological log of everyone who handled the evidence
questions.option_d: Date and time of evidence transfer
questions.option_e: List of remediation steps taken after evidence collection
questions.explanation: A custody record must identify every handler and the date and time of each transfer.

questions.question_text: A technician discovers evidence of credit card data theft on a company server. What is the most appropriate next step?
questions.option_a: Shut down the server to preserve its current state
questions.option_c: Disconnect the server from the network to prevent further access
questions.option_d: Notify management and follow escalation procedures
questions.explanation: Technicians should preserve evidence and use the approved management and incident-escalation path rather than improvise legal action.

questions.question_text: Which of the terms listed below is used to describe a forensic copy of a storage device that captures every sector of the drive, including deleted files, hidden partitions, and unallocated space?
questions.explanation: A bit-by-bit image captures allocated, deleted, hidden, and unallocated sectors rather than only visible files.

questions.question_text: Which of these external checks would be useful when troubleshooting a PC that shows no signs of receiving power?
questions.option_a: Ensure that the power cord is securely connected to both the wall outlet and the PSU
questions.option_b: Confirm that the outlet is delivering power by testing it with another device or using a circuit tester
questions.option_c: Examine the power cord for physical damage or fraying
questions.option_d: Verify that any surge protector or power strip is turned on and functioning properly
questions.option_e: Plug the system directly into the wall outlet to eliminate the surge protector as a factor
questions.explanation: Checking the outlet, cord, power strip, and a direct wall connection safely eliminates external power causes first.

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions might be of help when troubleshooting a PSU that fails to power on?
questions.option_a: Confirming that the PSU’s power switch (usually located on the back of the unit) is turned on
questions.option_b: Inspecting the PSU for any signs of physical damage, burning smells, or unusual noises
questions.option_c: Performing a paperclip test (ATX jumper test) to verify PSU fan activation
questions.option_d: Testing the PSU with a PSU tester or replacing it temporarily with a known-good unit
questions.explanation: After basic switch and damage checks, qualified technicians can use an approved PSU tester or known-good unit; exposed-conductor tests require proper training.

questions.question_text: Which internal power delivery checks would be useful when troubleshooting a PC that is not powering on?
questions.option_a: Performing a visual inspection of internal components for signs of damage, such as burnt components or leaking capacitors
questions.option_b: Ensuring that the motherboard is installed correctly with no grounding issues (e.g., misplaced standoffs)
questions.option_c: Confirming that the CPU is properly aligned, securely locked, free from damage and debris, and in optimal contact with the cooling solution
questions.option_d: Ensuring that all internal power connectors (main ATX, CPU, GPU, and any additional connectors) are firmly seated on the motherboard
questions.option_e: Verifying that the power button cable from the case is correctly connected to the appropriate motherboard header
questions.option_f: Trying a minimal boot configuration (CPU, GPU, and a single RAM module) to determine if any additional component is causing a conflict that prevents power from being delivered or recognized
questions.explanation: All listed checks can interrupt internal power delivery, so inspect seating, connectors, headers, shorts, and a minimal configuration methodically.

questions.question_text: Which motherboard-related issue can result in degraded performance without triggering errors or shutdowns?
questions.explanation: Degraded capacitors can destabilize voltage delivery and reduce performance before producing a clear boot error.

questions.question_text: During heavy multitasking in a workstation, a technician notices that the disk activity light remains almost constantly lit, even without any large file transfers. Applications load very slowly, and the overall system response is noticeably degraded. A performance monitoring tool confirms an unusually high level of paging, where data is frequently swapped to the disk. What is the most likely cause of this behavior?
questions.explanation: Heavy paging with constant disk activity is the classic sign that workload demand exceeds available RAM.

questions.question_text: What are the likely effects of mixing RAM modules of different sizes and speeds on system performance? (Select 2 answers)
questions.option_a: The system will use the total combined memory size of all installed RAM modules
questions.option_b: The system will automatically downgrade performance to the speed of the slowest RAM module
questions.option_c: The system will use only the fastest RAM module to compensate for slower performance
questions.option_d: The system will prioritize the RAM module with the highest capacity
questions.option_e: The result of mixing RAM modules of different sizes will not affect system performance
questions.explanation: Mixed modules normally contribute their capacity but operate at a mutually supported speed, often the slowest module's rate.

questions.question_text: A CPU is operating well below its advertised speed, resulting in slow system response. The BIOS displays the correct CPU model but reports a lower frequency than expected. Which setting could cause this behavior?
questions.explanation: Power-saving firmware settings can intentionally lower CPU frequency even when the processor is correctly identified.

questions.question_text: After upgrading a gaming PC with a high-performance GPU, the user notices sluggish in-game performance, system instability, unexpected shutdowns, and random reboots under heavy load. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: A new high-draw GPU can overload an undersized PSU, causing instability and shutdowns under load.

questions.question_text: In Microsoft Windows operating systems, the Performance tab in Windows Task Manager allows users to identify hardware components affecting system performance. In a similar fashion, Task Manager's Processes tab can be used to identify compute-intensive applications and processes that may be the cause of sluggish system performance.
questions.explanation: Task Manager's Performance and Processes tabs show resource pressure and the processes consuming those resources.

questions.question_text: Excessive dust buildup inside the computer case might be the cause of overheating, which in turn may lead to:
questions.explanation: Dust-restricted airflow can cause throttling, crashes, shutdowns, and eventually permanent heat damage.

questions.question_text: Which of the symptoms listed below is most likely a direct result of overheating?
questions.explanation: Protective random shutdowns are a direct and urgent symptom of excessive component temperature.

questions.question_text: What is thermal throttling in relation to CPU overheating?
questions.option_a: The CPU increasing fan speed to cool down
questions.option_b: The CPU reducing its operating speed to avoid damage
questions.option_c: The PSU reducing voltage to the CPU
questions.option_d: The CPU entering a low-power state to reduce energy consumption
questions.explanation: Thermal throttling reduces clock speed to limit heat and protect the processor.

questions.question_text: What is the most appropriate immediate action when a burning smell is detected coming from a computer case?
questions.option_a: Disconnect all external devices and peripherals
questions.option_b: Inspect physical components for burn marks or discoloration
questions.option_c: Disable performance-boosting features in the OS to mitigate heat
questions.option_d: Shut down the system and unplug it from a power source
questions.explanation: A burning smell requires immediate shutdown and power disconnection; inspection comes only after the system is safe.

questions.question_text: Which of the following could lead to unexpected shutdowns in a computer system?
questions.option_c: Memory errors or failing RAM modules
questions.explanation: Cooling, memory, power, and software faults can all produce unexpected shutdowns.

questions.question_text: Which of the actions listed below can help maintain system stability and prevent hardware-related crashes?
questions.option_a: Cleaning internal components with compressed air to remove dust buildup
questions.option_b: Replacing or reapplying CPU thermal paste as needed
questions.option_d: Installing a PSU that meets or exceeds power requirements
questions.explanation: Cleaning, thermal maintenance, memory diagnostics, and an adequately rated PSU all support stable operation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tools in Windows can help troubleshoot unresponsive apps and identify potential causes of application crashes?
questions.explanation: Task Manager, Event Viewer, and Reliability Monitor provide complementary evidence for application hangs and crashes.

questions.question_text: A user reports a popping sound from their computer, followed by it shutting down. What is the most probable cause?
questions.option_b: Power surge from the wall outlet
questions.explanation: A pop followed by immediate shutdown commonly indicates a failed or blown capacitor.

questions.question_text: A visual inspection of a motherboard reveals a capacitor with a rounded top. What is the best course of action?
questions.option_a: Use a voltage meter to test the capacitor's charge
questions.option_b: Gently press down on the top of the capacitor
questions.option_c: Ignore it unless the system starts showing problems
questions.option_d: Replace the motherboard or affected component
questions.explanation: A rounded or swollen capacitor is failed hardware; do not press or probe it—replace the affected component using approved repair procedures.

questions.question_text: What should be done if a computer’s system date and time reset every time it is powered off, despite being set correctly in the OS?
questions.explanation: A depleted CMOS battery commonly causes firmware clock settings to reset whenever external power is removed.
